## Ways to Participate {#participate}

```{=html}
<div class="pillar-grid">
  <div class="pillar-card"><span class="pillar-icon"><i class="bi bi-eye-fill"></i></span><h4>Observe</h4><p>Join the mailing list, attend KOL webinars, and follow sub-team activities with no commitment required.</p></div>
  <div class="pillar-card"><span class="pillar-icon"><i class="bi bi-pencil-fill"></i></span><h4>Contribute</h4><p>Co-author papers, review manuscripts, present at webinars, or bring expertise to a specific project.</p></div>
  <div class="pillar-card"><span class="pillar-icon"><i class="bi bi-award-fill"></i></span><h4>Lead</h4><p>Take on a sub-team leadership role. The Leadership Team provides mentorship and support for new leads.</p></div>
  <div class="pillar-card"><span class="pillar-icon"><i class="bi bi-plus-circle-fill"></i></span><h4>Start Something New</h4><p>Prepare a one-page concept and meet with the leadership team to discuss scope, fit, and support for a new sub-team.</p></div>
</div>
```

## Open Positions &amp; Active Recruitment {#recruiting}

- **Master Protocol Regulatory Sub-team**, Volunteers for the 2020–2025 Systematic Literature Review update (full-text review, data extraction). Contact Peter Mesenbrink or Julia Niewczas.
- **Patient Engagement Sub-team**, Seeking a new sub-team leader to champion the integration of patient perspectives into innovative trial design. Open to patient advocates, clinical researchers, and methodologists with a patient-centered focus. Contact Mercedeh Ghadessi.
- **Concept, Methodology and Framework Sub-team (MPWG)**, Undergoing a reboot under Bryan McComb and Courtney Henry. New members welcome. Contact either directly.
- **Patient advocates and patient organizations**, The IDSWG specifically welcomes patient advocates as full members. If your organization works in rare diseases or another area where the group is active, we'd like to hear from you.
